repository.name: @webex/plugin-authorization-browser-first-party
repository.purpose: Browser OAuth 2.0 authorization plugin for the first-party Webex Web Client. It registers webex.authorization, completes the Authorization Code + PKCE redirect during SDK initialization (CSRF state check, URL scrubbing, preauth catalog hint, token exchange), starts first-party and third-party (social provider) login redirects, runs the Device Authorization (QR code) polling flow, and supplies public/confidential client authentication for the token exchange and refresh callback.

The one WEAK field is test strategy: test/unit/spec/authorization.js has 73 passing cases after build:src, but plugin registration and proxies, the 400 grant-error mapping, the logout redirect, the shared event emitter, and a 400 polling response without a body have no test, the suite imports the default export from dist, the browser suite is describe.skip, and no characterization baseline exists. authz-bfp-sdk.summary: Published npm package. main is dist/index.js and devMain is src/index.js. Importing the package registers the Authorization plugin as public plugin 'authorization' with the config object from src/config.js and proxies isAuthorizing and isAuthenticating onto the webex instance. The barrel exports the plugin class as default, Events, InitialAuthorizationCodeGrantOutcomes, and config. Instance methods, properties, and config keys are described in src/docs/README.md.

authz-bfp-events.summary: Events emitted on webex.authorization.eventEmitter (a Node EventEmitter): 'login' with eventType initiateLogin or redirectToLoginUrl, and 'qRCodeLogin' with eventType getUserCodeSuccess, getUserCodeFailure, authorizationPending, authorizationSuccess, authorizationFailure, or pollingCanceled. Event names are exported as Events.

authz-bfp-redirect-protocol.summary: Browser redirect round-trip owned by the plugin: base64url-JSON state carrying csrf_token and emailhash; sessionStorage keys oauth2-csrf-token and oauth2-code-verifier; callback query parameters code, state, error, id_token, and email; PKCE S256 code_challenge; and the authorization_code token-exchange form posted to config.tokenUrl.

webex-core-plugin-host.summary: registerPlugin (first registration of a name wins unless replace is set; config is merged; proxies become derived properties; webex.ready depends on authorization.ready), WebexPlugin (config resolved from webex.config.credentials through the Credentials namespace, logger, request), credentials.buildLoginUrl / buildThirdPartyLoginUrl / buildLogoutUrl / set({supertoken}), grantErrors.select, services.collectPreauthCatalog and services.get('oauth-helper'), webex.getWindow, and WebexCore.logout calling authorization.logout. Owned by @webex/webex-core, which has no SDD spec.

webex-common-js-api.summary: oneFlight and whileInFlight method decorators and the encodeState/decodeState base64url JSON codec, as specified by the @webex/common module spec.

idbroker-oauth.source: Cisco IdBroker OAuth 2.0 endpoints configured through webex.config.credentials (authorizeUrl, tokenUrl, logoutUrl, thirdPartyLoginUrl in packages/@webex/webex-core/src/credentials-config.js)
idbroker-oauth.summary: Authorization endpoint (response_type=code with PKCE S256 and state), token endpoint (authorization_code and refresh_token grants, self_contained_token), logout endpoint, and the /idb/ThirdPartyLogin social-provider hand-off. Owned by the identity service, not by this repository.

oauth-helper-device-authorization.source: Webex oauth-helper service from the service catalog (resources /actions/device/authorize and /actions/device/token)
oauth-helper-device-authorization.summary: Device Authorization grant: POST /actions/device/authorize returns device_code, user_code, verification_uri, verification_uri_complete, interval, expires_in; POST /actions/device/token with grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code returns tokens, 428 while pending, or 400 slow_down. Both calls use HTTP Basic client authentication.
